title: sse: fix partial-JSON streaming framing and delimiter ordering
author: Alyssa Chen
description: Summary: Fixes multiple SSE streaming edge cases that caused malformed partial-JSON payloads and out-of-order token/event framing observed in long-lived streaming responses. Motivation: production incidents and internal fuzzing identified two related classes of bugs: (1) delimiter ordering between 'data:' event boundaries and JSON token chunks which could result in malformed partial JSON delivered to clients, and (2) a race between buffer flushes and framing metadata that could emit closing delimiters before the last JSON token was written. This patch ensures deterministic ordering and safe buffering for partial JSON payloads across our OpenAI compatibility layer and the native /v1/streams SSE handler. Change details: - Normalize event emission order so that framing delimiters (event start/end) are always emitted outside of token-level writes. - Add a small per-connection flush lock to prevent buffer flush races when the generator finishes mid-token. - Emit explicit chunk delimiters for partial-JSON arrays ("[", ",", "]") in a stable producer-side order when streaming structured output (tools/functions). - Update the OpenAI-compat shim to follow the same ordering so downstream SDKs receive consistent events. - Add unit + integration tests that reproduce the original failures (partial JSON array split across multiple chunks; trailing delimiter emitted before last token). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for token ordering and delimiter emission - [x] Integration test using sse-harness replicating reported SUP-1192 trace - [x] Updated OpenAI compatibility adapter tests - [x] Manual canary on staging for 48h - [x] Docs update / changelog entry Comments on scope: This PR intentionally keeps the fix focused to framing and ordering logic (no kernel/runtime perf changes). Follow-ups: a) audit continuous-batching flush paths for the same race in other protocols (ENG-4703), b) consider exposing a strict "sse_structured_streaming" flag to allow older clients to opt into legacy ordering for compatibility.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz (review): The root cause looks like a race between buffer.flush() and the event emission path. Can we keep the lock scoped to finalization only? Avoid broad locks that may impact throughput.
Alyssa Chen (author): Good call — lock is scoped to finalization path and microbenchmarks show <0.25% p50 throughput regression in stressed e2e. Added a comment in buffer.py explaining scope.
Devin Patel (review): Please add an integration test that reproduces the exact SUP-1192 event trace — I want the CI to catch regressions.
Alyssa Chen (author): Added sse_harness test that uses the same chunking and timing as the incident trace. CI fuzz corpus also contains the failing trace.
Sara Li (approval): Verified on staging canary (48h) — no regressions observed. Approving for merge.
ci_checks: ci/integration: initially failed (reproduced SUP-1192), rerun after fix: passed
release_notes: SSE streaming: fixed partial-JSON framing and delimiter ordering bugs that could produce malformed partial-JSON responses for long-lived streams. No breaking changes. (ENG-4621, SUP-1192)
reproduction_steps: 1) Start a structured streaming request that returns a JSON array of tool-calls / functions and streams tokens across multiple chunks. 2) Use the sse-harness with artificial chunk boundaries so the '[' and first object tokens arrive in separate buffer flushes. 3) Observe malformed JSON when delimiter ']' or ',' is emitted before final token. The included integration test reproduces this exact sequence.
testing_notes: Added unit tests for delimiter ordering, integration test that reproduces SUP-1192, and fuzz regression corpus. Manual canary run on staging for 48h with request volume similar to customer trace. Added comments and microbench numbers to buffer.py.
